policy.description: European Spanish contains systematic pronunciation variation. IberoLab will not collapse it into an unnamed default or infer a speaker profile from spelling alone.

documented_dimensions.description: Relationship among the phonological values associated with written s, z and c before e/i.

options.description: Maintain a phonological contrast between /s/ and the interdental sibilant used for z and c before e/i.
Use /s/ for both orthographic series. This is a fully accepted pronunciation in the areas where it is established.
Use the interdental sibilant for both orthographic series; this option requires an explicitly scoped profile and sociolinguistic review.

sources.citation: Real Academia Española y Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española, El seseo y el ceceo, El buen uso del español.
sources.scope: Geographic distribution, contrast, seseo, ceceo and sociolinguistic qualification.

sources.citation: Martínez-Celdrán, Fernández-Planas and Carrera-Sabaté, Castilian Spanish, Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(2), 2003.
sources.scope: Formal Castilian reference description with distinction; not a universal European Spanish profile.

documented_dimensions.description: Whether orthographic y and ll share one consonantal phoneme or preserve a contrast involving the palatal lateral.

options.description: Treat consonantal y and ll as the same phonological category, without fixing a single allophonic realization.
Preserve a contrast between consonantal y and the palatal lateral represented by ll.

sources.citation: Real Academia Española y Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española, Ortografía básica de la lengua española, section on y, ll and yeísmo.
sources.scope: Definition of yeísmo and acknowledgment that it predominates across much of the Spanish-speaking territory.

sources.citation: Martínez-Celdrán, Fernández-Planas and Carrera-Sabaté, Castilian Spanish, Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(2), 2003.
sources.scope: Reference description of a formal Castilian variety and its palatal categories.

documented_dimensions.description: Whether adjacent vowels are realized within one syllable or across a hiatus when actual pronunciation can vary among speakers or words.

options.description: A reviewed lexical entry specifies a diphthongal realization.
A reviewed lexical entry specifies a hiatus.
A reviewed profile rule supplies the realization for a delimited environment.
Preserve both analyses without ranking when pronunciation is not fixed by approved evidence.

sources.citation: Real Academia Española y Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española, Ortografía de la lengua española, treatment of diphthongs, triphthongs and hiatuses.
sources.scope: Distinction between orthographic conventions and actual pronunciation, including variable vowel sequences.

documented_dimensions.description: Source used to identify lexical stress before phonetic adaptation.

options.description: Use explicit accent marks and a reviewed lexical entry, recording any exception.
Require a user-supplied pronunciation when the input is exceptional, foreign, abbreviated or otherwise unresolved.
Preserve multiple stress analyses without ranking when no approved source resolves them.

sources.citation: Real Academia Española y Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española, Ortografía de la lengua española, sections on prosodic and graphic accent.
sources.scope: Prosodic stress, graphic accent and the limits of deriving pronunciation from spelling alone.

reference_descriptions.description: Peer-reviewed illustration of a formal Castilian variety. It may inform notation and testing but must not be treated as the unnamed default for all European Spanish speakers.
reference_descriptions.citation: Martínez-Celdrán, Fernández-Planas and Carrera-Sabaté, Castilian Spanish, Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(2), 2003.

pending_dimensions.reason: Requires geographically scoped primary sources and a decision about lexical versus connected-speech depth.
Requires register, lexical and geographic scope before options can be normalized.
Requires a reviewed European Spanish regional model and explicit phonetic notation.
Requires a separate treatment of phonemic contrast, allophony and reduction.
Requires a reviewed lexicon and a user-supplied pronunciation policy.
